newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INTERVIEW-Refocused S.African Sanlam eyes Asia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Refocused S.African Sanlam eyes Asia.

text.p: South Africa's Sanlam investment corporation will look to the Indian Ocean rim and Southeast Asia for new markets for its refocused operations, chairman Marinus Daling said.

Daling said in an interview ahead of the mutual company's annual meeting on Wednesday that Sanlam, the country's second biggest life assurer, would reduce its controlling interests in non-financial companies over the next two years to normal portfolio levels.
"The company will go from life assurance to financial services, which will include things like more emphasis on unit trusts, managed health care and trust business," he said.
Daling said Sanlam would address the pressure from foreign competitors coming into South Africa since the transition to democracy three years ago by focusing on core activities.
"We will start off by making investments in other countries to serve the current South African client base...Thereafter, I also believe that we will look for clients in other countries."
Daling said Sanlam would reduce its holdings in companies including Gencor Ltd, Murray and Roberts, Sentrachem and companies emerging from the proposed unbundling of Malbak and Servgro.

"Just selling down on the stock exchange would be a short-term view. Our emphasis is rather on adding value also through the building down process. I think it will be transaction driven...with a significant element of international investment."
Daling said Sanlam would look for more effective operational alliances with financial partners, but without significant increases in its effectively controlling interests in Santam, Gensec and ABSA.
The priority over the next year would be to benchmark Sanlam's investment and operational performances internationally before seeking alliances with partners abroad.
He said, however, that the company had not yet identified potential partners or specific markets in which it could become internationally competitive.

"I would say that in the asset management side, you have to be in the financial centres of the world. In providing our services to markets, I believe that the emerging market may have better opportunities for us than the mature markets.
"I believe that we have skills in transferring the abilities of the first world financial services to emerging markets and the new wealth that they will be generating."
The major opportunities in the financial services area were probably situated on the Indian Ocean rim and the ASEAN countries, he said.
"Africa will follow, but I think Africa still has some way to go to create the opportunities that we already see in those markets.
"It's a question of sequencing. Eventually, if we can do well in some of those emerging markets, it will just enhance our ability to also do well in Africa," he said.
